title: Natural variability of maximal bite-, and tongue force over time in healthy young adults by isometric force measurement
summary: In this study we measure isometric bite-, and tongue force in healthy patients over time. A method for measuring bite-, and tonge force, is an important tool in the monitoring of patients with neuromuscular diseases like spinal muscle atrophy (SMA). This monitoring over time can show us if and how neuromuscluar medications influence oral function. Measuring oral function in healthy patients may help us to interpret data of morbid patients.

interventions.name: Healthy volunteers without muscular diseases, skelettal Trauma, craniomandibular dysfunction or periodontal diseases, are accompanied over a period of approximately 300 days. At specified time points, the maximum bite-, and tongue force and enduramce time are measured by using a piezoelectric sensor

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-patients of the Department of orthodontics aged ≥ 14 years
-existence of the declaration of consent for the study
-complete dentition in the posterior region
Exclusion criteria:
No consent of the patient.
Condylar or muscular complaints in the stomatognathic system (Craniomandibular
dysfunction).
Patients with neuromuscular diseases.
General medical findings with muscle hyper- or hypotension.
Ankyglossia.
Skelettal Trauma (jaw).
Parodontal diseases.
Lack of ability to consent.
Multiple missing teeth in the posterior region.
